goals: Maintain the progression-gated one-way return system for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric using one shared placed Dragonbound Waystone, an Imbued Void Pearl, and a cooldown-based Dragonbound Staff.

Preserve the accepted server-owned channel, exact-destination safety, persistent anchor, loss protection, recipes, configuration migration, discovery behavior, geometry, and art while allowing one eligible building block identity to select the Waystone's visual material without expanding into a general waypoint or teleport system.
scope: Canary 15's selectable-material renderer uses one persistent block-id material component, a two-input dynamic crafting recipe, and client-only baked-model wrappers that retain the accepted four-cuboid Waystone geometry. The supplied runtime observation is limited to that material implementation working as expected; it does not establish a broader runtime pass or owner acceptance.

Canary 16's supplied runtime FAIL is limited to its successful-arrival sound lookup crash: its `enderscape:mirror.teleport` lookup was not registered by the exact pinned Enderscape 3.0.2 input. Canary 17 corrects that normal successful-arrival lookup to `enderscape:item.mirror.teleport`. Canary 18 preserves that exact normal presentation for every successful return and, only after the existing teleport, exact-arrival, and held-source-item gates, adds Enderscape 3.0.2's own default lodestone overlay/vignette packet (`enderscape:misc/overlay` and `enderscape:misc/vignette`, 60 client ticks) plus its local `enderscape:item.mirror.transdimensional_travel` payload sound when the captured starting dimension differs from the Waystone destination. It neither adds `mirror_teleport_out` nor alters Dragonbound's channel buildup, teleport mechanics, consumption, cooldown, or success message.

Canary 19 replaces the insufficient same-state block dirtiness on client `visual_material` synchronization with Minecraft 26.2's public `ClientLevel.setSectionRangeDirty` call whose equal section-range endpoints rebuild exactly the Waystone's rendered chunk section. It retains the material-only update packet, server-owned placed stack, four-cuboid material-retargeting renderer, and component-less End Stone Bricks fallback.

Preserve the 40-tick default channel, 1,200-tick Staff cooldown, existing primary recipes plus the dynamic material recipe, one-click and mouse-release-independent channel lifecycle, exact arrival at the visible Waystone top, recipe-book and JEI discovery seam, and success-only consumption and cooldown behavior.
Retain exact accepted Canary 5 and focused-runtime-passed Canary 4 rollback artifacts together with the Dragonbound-owned Staff art and the separately licensed Matcha Stable Void snapshot and notice.

exclusions: Multiple destinations, waypoint lists, portals, home commands, arbitrary coordinates, nearby-position fallback, XP costs, durability, charges, pet or group teleport, and other feature or balance changes.

Changes to Waystone collision/shape, teleport and anchor authority, channel timing, Staff/Pearl behavior, loss protection, existing primary recipes, configuration, art, or unrelated scope beyond Canary 18's post-gate cross-dimension Enderscape Mirror presentation.
Mod Menu polish and dedicated-server validation remain deferred; the accepted evidence is the recorded client and singleplayer scope only.
Other projects and their source, status, artifacts, dependencies, and ownership records remain outside this project.

Minecraft deployment, either experimental Test Slot, accepted physical-baseline changes, Test Instance Manager mutation, Minecraft launch, and protected gameplay-instance access during this migration.
Redistribution of the embedded Matcha/Klei bitmap without independently satisfying its CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 attribution, non-commercial, and share-alike terms.

state.milestone: The supplied runtime failure for current Canary 18 is limited to materialized Waystone placement rendering: a non-default material initially appears as End Stone Bricks, then becomes correct after an unrelated neighboring block update. This demonstrates client material identity synchronization but insufficient same-state geometry invalidation; no other failure is inferred. Canary 19 explicitly invalidates only the changed Waystone's client render section after `visual_material` changes. Canary 12 remains accepted; Canary 19 awaits focused Minecraft runtime verification.

exceptions.reason: Canary 18 resolves Enderscape's effective normal and transdimensional Mirror sound IDs, teleport-IN particle registry, and its own default lodestone overlay/vignette packet for the required post-gate presentation.
regression_evidence: The build and focused static contracts fail closed unless enderscape-fabric-3.0.2+mc26.2.jar matches SHA-256 9fcc4f59ca88e91f90e7c7d18289f2f859f20c810eebcca924764aa15236c40b.

The focused contract verifies that Enderscape's item-sound registration prefix resolves literal mirror.teleport and mirror.transdimensional_travel holder arguments to final registry IDs enderscape:item.mirror.teleport and enderscape:item.mirror.transdimensional_travel; it also verifies the default lodestone visual payload route, same-dimension exclusion, exact post-teleport/arrival/held-item ordering, cancellation/failure exclusion, no mirror_teleport_out use, no Enderman success sound, and no old success-only portal bursts.

accepted.summary: Maintains a progression-gated one-way return system using a Dragonbound Waystone and Staff.
